text:
tom: Heads-up - we promoted TS SDK v2.4.0 about 5m ago. Initial smoke looked fine, but we're seeing a growing number of serialization errors reported by downstream integration tests (internal infra). tagging this thread for rollback coordination if needed.

nina: saw the alerts. sample error: "TypeError: Cannot read property 'toJSON' of undefined" coming from client.serializeRequest() when optional metadata is omitted. Repro locally with sample app.

lucas: confirmed. regression introduced by the new request wrapper in 2.4.0 that assumes metadata exists. I can push a quick patch (2.4.1) but we need to decide: immediate rollback vs patch-forward. Thoughts?

release-bot: [monitor] 2.4.0 live at 'latest' since 22:18 UTC. Error rate increase: from 0.05% -> 1.2% in the last 3m. Affected services: integrations-runner, billing-sync tests.

infra: recommendation: pin TS to previous dist-tag immediately to stop new installs pulling the bad package. Steps below.

``` 
# pin to previous
npm dist-tag add @redwood/sdk@2.3.0 latest
# deprecate problematic release to surface message
npm deprecate @redwood/sdk@2.4.0 "rollback: serialization regression, use 2.3.0 or wait for 2.4.1"
```

product: we need messaging for customers. We'll prepare a short status note: impacted internal integrations and some downstream open-source connectors may hit errors; we're rolling back TS and will follow up with patch. Claire please draft.

claire: drafting now. propose: one-line alert on status page + email to active SDK users with mitigation (use explicit metadata object until patch lands).

tom: quick ops decision required: do we pin now and publish 2.4.1 later, or let 2.4.1 cut and promote immediately? Risk: more installs in the next 30m. I lean pin now.

lucas: patch is ready locally (small guard in serializeRequest). I can publish 2.4.1 within 10m, but propagation takes time. Pin now, publish patch, test, then promote in safe window.

release-bot: [action] Creating rollback job: 3302027890-rb1. Will pin dist-tag and deprecate 2.4.0 if approved.

nina: one caveat: internal cached images reference the 'latest' dist-tag for automated builds. Pinning should prevent new pulls but won't fix already cached images. We'll need to trigger a rebuild for critical pipelines.

infra: we can queue rebuild on the affected runners; estimated 12m to complete for high-priority ones. We'll prioritize billing-sync.

product: deploy message snippet: "We've paused the TS SDK rollout (v2.4.0) due to a serialization regression affecting some integrations. Use v2.3.0 while we publish a patch. We'll update within 30 minutes." Approve?

claire: approved. I'll send to status and support with triage steps.

release-bot: [execute] Pinning @redwood/sdk to 2.3.0 as 'latest' and deprecating 2.4.0.

release-bot: npm commands executed. Dist-tag updated. Deprecation message set.

tom: thanks. Lucas, publish 2.4.1 and post the publish job here with smoke results. Also include exact file changes for the changelog so release notes reflect the rollback and fix.

lucas: publishing 2.4.1-canary now, will run smoke. Patch notes: 
- fix: guard against missing metadata in serializeRequest
- chore: add unit test for missing metadata case

release-bot: [publish-job] 2.4.1-canary published. Canary smoke running against integrations-runner.

nina: smoke: 5/5 tests passed for canonical flows. No serialization errors seen in canary. Latency similar.

lucas: okay pushing final 2.4.1 to npm as prerelease, will wait 5m then promote if stable.

infra: rebuild of cached images started for affected pipelines. ETA ~10m.

product: sending status update now: includes mitigation steps for customers and timeline (patch in progress, pin in place).

claire: support ticket template added with reproduction steps and recommended temporary fix (explicit metadata).

release-bot: [monitor] Post-pin installs show immediate drop in 2.4.0 adoption. Error rate trending down to baseline.

tom: once canary is stable, we'll flip latest to 2.4.1 and mark release notes updated: include an item about the rollback and the root cause. Any objections to that flow?

nina: no objections. request that we include a short blurb for OSS integrators on why explicit metadata is safer.

lucas: will include. promoting in 4m if canary remains green.

release-bot: Canary stable at 22:52 UTC. Promoting 2.4.1 to 'latest' in 3...2...1.

release-bot: Promotion complete. @redwood/sdk@2.4.1 is now 'latest'. Previous 2.4.0 remains deprecated.

infra: rebuilding completed for critical pipelines. Roll-forward verified.

product: status page updated: incident resolved, follow-up postmortem to be posted tomorrow.

claire: sending customer outreach now.

lucas: pushing final changelog entry and closing the release checklist.

release-bot: [announce] TS SDK rollback-handled & patch released. Thread closed. :white_check_mark:
